patient_actor_hidden.History: The patient reports experiencing fever, chills, and a headache starting three days after undergoing an open cholecystectomy. She has a history of an abdominal hysterectomy 16 years ago. She has been smoking one pack of cigarettes daily for 17 years.

Symptoms.Primary_Symptom: Right-sided chest pain that increases on inspiration
Secondary_Symptoms: Productive cough for the last 12 hours

Social_History.Smoking_Status: Current smoker, one pack daily for 17 years

Review_of_Systems.Gastrointestinal: Surgical site below right ribcage, otherwise unremarkable

objective_for_doctor: Evaluate the patient presenting with postoperative fever, chest pain that increases on inspiration, and a productive cough, and determine the correct diagnosis.

turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Doctor: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today? Patient: I had an open cholecystectomy three days ago, and since then I’ve developed fever, chills, and a headache. I also have right-sided chest pain that gets worse when I take a deep breath, along with a productive cough for the past 12 hours.
Do you feel short of breath at rest?
Patient: I feel short of breath, especially when I’m moving around, but at rest it’s not too bad. I still have the fever and the pain on the right side when I breathe in deeply.
What color is the sputum you're coughing up—clear, white, yellow, green, or bloody?
Patient: It’s yellowish sputum, and I’ve been coughing it up since it started about 12 hours ago.
Do you have any abdominal pain, particularly in the right upper quadrant, or pain in your right shoulder?

Patient: Yes, I have some discomfort around the incision area below my right ribcage, but I don’t notice pain that shoots to my right shoulder. I haven’t had much right upper quadrant pain beyond the surgical site.
Is the surgical incision showing any redness, warmth, swelling, or drainage (pus or fluid leaking from the wound)?
Patient: Yes, the incision area is a bit warm and tender, but I don’t see a lot of spreading redness. I haven’t noticed pus, but there’s some mild drainage on the dressing.
Are you experiencing any yellowing of your skin or eyes, or has your urine become darker than usual?

Patient: No, I haven’t noticed any yellowing of my skin or eyes, and my urine doesn’t look darker than usual. I’m mainly bothered by the fever and chills, the yellowish cough, and the right-sided chest pain when I breathe deeply.
Do you have any pain, swelling, or tenderness in your calves, particularly in the leg that may have been immobilized during surgery?

Patient: I don’t have any noticeable pain, swelling, or tenderness in either of my calves, and I haven’t felt any leg discomfort since the surgery. I’m mainly having fever and chills, plus the right-sided chest pain that worsens when I take a deep breath.
When you take a deep breath, do you feel pain only in your chest, or do you also feel pain deep in your upper abdomen below the right ribs?
Patient: It’s mostly just in the right side of my chest, and it gets sharper when I take a deep breath—I don’t really feel it deep in my upper abdomen below my right ribs.
Have you checked your oxygen level with a pulse oximeter, or have you noticed if your heart is racing unusually fast?
Patient: I haven’t checked my oxygen level with a pulse oximeter, but my heart feels like it’s beating faster than usual when the fever is up. I’m not sure exactly how fast it is, though.
Have you noticed any blood in your sputum when you cough, even just small streaks?

Patient: No, I haven’t noticed any blood or blood streaks in my sputum—just the yellowish mucus. My main issues are the fever and chills, the yellowish cough, and the sharp right chest pain when I breathe in.
[DDX] Post-operative pneumonia (right lower lobe), Pulmonary embolism, Subphrenic abscess, Surgical site infection (cellulitis), Atelectasis with secondary infection
